title: Fitzwilliam Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works shaped by thresholds, enclosed spaces and the things left between figures.
introduction:
The Annunciation takes place across an interval. Gabriel and Mary occupy separate sides of the courtyard, while the architecture leads attention beyond them. A Rossetti encounter has almost the opposite difficulty: two resembling couples occupy a wood too crowded to keep their identities comfortably apart. Both pictures make space part of the event rather than a neutral container for it.

Other works in this selection need far less narrative. A cup and saucer can occupy an entire painting; boats can establish a lagoon with only sparse accents. Following these changes of scale is one way to read the collection without asking every work to declare its historical importance.
visitNote: This selection is not a fixed route through the Fitzwilliam. Works on paper rotate and paintings may be on loan or in storage. The coloured version of Rossetti’s How They Met Themselves is distinct from the museum’s separate ink drawing; this guide discusses the coloured work.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: Ruskin’s exercises in noticing edges, tones and natural forms accompany both the detailed nineteenth-century pictures and the more economical watercolours. They encourage returning to a particular visible feature before making a broad judgment.

works.title: The Bridesmaid
works.credit: John Everett Millais. The Bridesmaid. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The mass of red hair makes a strong first boundary around the face, but the small action of the hands also calls for attention. Foreground objects and dark space behind keep the figure close. Millais lets an intimate gesture compete with a conspicuous surface, so that the portrait-like presence does not exhaust the scene.

works.title: The Annunciation
works.catalogueTitle: The Annunciation, predella panel from the St. Lucy Altarpiece
works.credit: Domenico Veneziano. The Annunciation, predella panel from the St. Lucy Altarpiece. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The passage between Gabriel and Mary makes their separation conspicuous. It also draws attention toward a closed door beyond. The museum notes that the panel was trimmed on the left, disturbing its original architectural symmetry. Its present balance should therefore be read as the surviving arrangement of an altered object, not an untouched geometrical ideal.

works.title: The Miracle of Saint Zenobius
works.credit: Domenico Veneziano. The Miracle of St. Zenobius. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The street gives the bishop, child and surrounding figures defined positions from which to act and respond. Architecture helps separate their gestures without dispersing the episode. This panel and the *Annunciation* once belonged to the same altarpiece’s lower strip, or predella; their small scenes had a place beneath a much larger sacred image.

works.title: The Nativity
works.credit: Domenico Ghirlandaio. The Nativity. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Overlapping heads and hands gather closely around the child. The shelter and animals keep the foreground compact, even though a landscape continues beyond it. Ghirlandaio makes attention itself the group’s shared action: the surrounding figures are linked by where they look and kneel rather than a sequence of dramatic movements.

works.title: How They Met Themselves
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. How They Met Themselves. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/dante-gabriel-rossetti/how-they-met-themselves-1864
works.description: The encounter depends on resemblance. A couple meets another pair like themselves, and the wood has little room to separate the doubled bodies. Crossed hands and swords intensify that crowding. The familiar becomes difficult precisely because it recurs where it should not: the painting’s disturbance is built from recognition rather than an unidentifiable monster.

works.title: Joan of Arc
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Joan of Arc. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The sword rises near Joan’s face while her gaze turns upward. Metal and rich fabric give the close figure physical substance, but the gesture interrupts any straightforward action of combat. Armour establishes a martial role; the direction of attention complicates it, keeping devotion and military equipment within the same confined view.

works.title: Girl at a Lattice
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Girl at a Lattice. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/dante-gabriel-rossetti/girl-at-a-lattice-1862
works.description: The window is a boundary without a disclosed destination. The woman leans close to its ledge, yet her turned face prevents a simple exchange of looks with the spectator. Flowers add a near, tangible presence. What lies beyond the threshold remains less definite than the position of the figure beside it.

works.title: Golden Water
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Golden Water. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/dante-gabriel-rossetti/golden-water-1858
works.description: The dark vessel has weight because the woman’s arms contain it against her body. Hair, pale clothing and plants extend the upright arrangement around that central relation. The title may promise a narrative, but the image is largely still; its clearest information is how a person holds an object.

works.title: Portrait of an Unknown Man
works.credit: Frans Hals. Portrait of an Unknown Man. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The face addresses the spectator more directly than the loosely handled grey garment describes every fold. A broad black hat gives the head a firm setting. Hals lets differing degrees of finish coexist: the clothing remains a field of strokes while the likeness holds together as a particular presence.

works.title: The Lagoon towards Murano from the Fondamenta Nuove
works.catalogueTitle: The Lagoon Looking toward Murano from the Fondamenta Nuove
works.credit: Francesco Guardi. The Lagoon Looking toward Murano from the Fondamenta Nuove. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/francesco-guardi/the-lagoon-looking-toward-murano-from-the-fondamenta-nuove-1770
works.description: Architecture is reduced to low marks along the horizon, leaving water and grey sky much more room. Boats and slender masts keep that openness from becoming unlocated. Guardi makes a city recognisable without a monumental façade dominating the view: the lagoon and the intervals between its small accents carry Venice here.

works.title: White Cup and Saucer
works.credit: Henri Fantin-Latour. White Cup And Saucer. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-fantin-latour/white-cup-and-saucer-1864
works.description: The cup does not need an elaborate setting. Its rim, handle and rounded body divide white into different conditions of light, with the saucer and spoon offering a few related shapes. Isolation gives those distinctions enough attention to sustain the painting; the everyday vessel is neither hidden in a feast nor required to symbolise one.

works.title: Working the Land
works.credit: Working the land. WikiArt; Paul Gauguin. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The workers and animals remain within broad stretches of cultivated ground. Trees, low buildings and sky connect their labour to a continuous place. For readers who associate Gauguin with later, flatter arrangements, this early landscape is a useful complication: an artist’s name does not guarantee one unchanging way of constructing a scene.

works.title: Lindisfarne
works.credit: Thomas Girtin. Lindisfarne. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/thomas-girtin/lindisfarne-1798
works.description: The sky enters the ruin through the missing masonry as well as above its surviving walls. Those openings are essential to the view’s structure. Girtin distinguishes stone from air without needing to reconstruct the building intact; the losses give the remaining arches their particular rhythm and exposure.

works.title: Hydrangeas
works.credit: Philip Wilson Steer. Hydrangeas. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Flowers, clothing and surroundings nearly share one busy pattern of light and marks. The reaching hand and face keep the woman’s activity readable within it. Steer allows that balance to remain close: enough distinction to follow a person reaching, enough continuity for the figure to belong to the same surface as the hydrangeas.

works.title: The Three Marys at the Empty Sepulchre
works.catalogueTitle: The Three Marys at the Empty Sepulchre
works.credit: Giovanni Battista Gaulli. The Three Marys at the Empty Sepulchre. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/giovanni-battista-gaulli/the-three-maries-at-the-empty-sepulchre
works.description: Hands direct attention toward an absence. Women approach while angels indicate the tomb, requiring the vacant place to carry the scene’s discovery. Colour helps keep the figures distinct, but gesture makes their relations intelligible. The event depends less on what occupies the centre than on how the group responds to what is missing.

works.title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
works.credit: Luis Tristán. The Adoration of the Shepherds. Image credit: Luis Tristán; Art UK. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Luis_Trist%C3%A1n_de_Escamilla_(1585-1624)_-_The_Adoration_of_the_Shepherds_-_M.78_-_Fitzwilliam_Museum.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The child anchors a dense gathering that continues upward into angels and darkness. Faces and bright cloth keep returning attention to particular bodies within the crowd. Light has an organising task: without its uneven distribution, the many figures could compete equally and weaken the concentration around the newborn.

works.title: The Tombs of the Sultans near Cairo
works.catalogueTitle: The Tombs of the Sultans near Cairo
works.credit: Elijah Walton. The Tombs of the Sultans near Cairo. Image credit: Elijah Walton; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The monuments occupy less space than the sunset above them. Darker tracks and rough foreground ground lead toward a view whose principal change is in the sky. Walton gives the architecture a time and atmosphere, rather than isolating each structure as an object that could be removed from its surroundings.

works.title: The Andrews Family
works.credit: James Wills. The Andrews Family. Image credit: James Wills; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Five people share a terrace, but their heights and turns vary. The family relation is carried by that common space and coordinated presentation rather than a row of equivalent poses. Trees and landscape supply a setting large enough to hold them together while keeping seated and standing figures distinct.

works.title: Maria Isabel de Borbón, Queen of the Two Sicilies
works.catalogueTitle: Maria Isabel du Boubón, Queen of the Two Sicilies
works.credit: Vicente López Portaña. Maria Isabel du Boubón, Queen of the Two Sicilies. Image credit: Vicente López Portaña; Art UK. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vicente_L%C3%B3pez_Porta%C3%B1a_(1772-1850)_-_Mar%C3%ADa_Isabel_de_Borb%C3%B3n,_Queen_of_the_Two_Sicilies_-_PD.254-2015_-_Fitzwilliam_Museum.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The elaborate sleeves and headwear, dark dress and red fabric establish a ceremonial setting around the queen. A supported hand helps maintain the controlled standing pose. The extensive display is organised around a face, keeping public rank and individual likeness in relation rather than allowing either to account for the portrait alone.

works.title: Unknown Man
works.credit: Charles Beale. Unknown man (1693). Image credit: Charles Beale; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The sitter’s name is unknown, but the portrait is not consequently unspecific. The turn of the head, white neckcloth and warm brown robe establish a particular arrangement against darkness. Light gathers at face and chest, making a directed presence available even where the historical identification has been lost.

closingSections.title: Leave room for what is not shown
paragraphs: Compare the empty passage in the *Annunciation*, the vacant tomb in Gaulli and the indefinite view beyond Rossetti’s window. Their gaps do different work. These comparisons need not follow gallery order; check the Fitzwilliam’s current information if a particular painting or work on paper is central to a visit.
